row.evidence: Google's Looker (Google Cloud core) docs say to remove access "by applying changes to the authentication method" (IdP or IAM), and SAML creates users on first login; no SCIM endpoint is documented.
row.notes: New row. Looker is sold today as Looker (Google Cloud core) in Standard, Enterprise and Embed editions, all "Call sales" with annual commitments (each includes 10 Standard and 2 Developer users); no list prices, so team and SSO price fields stay null. SAML and OpenID Connect authentication are available on Looker (Google Cloud core) (feature table, no edition gate); SAML sign-in creates a new Looker user when none exists (JIT), and new-user groups/roles apply at first login. No SCIM is documented: Google recommends removing access in the IdP (or IAM for Google OAuth), after which the Looker user still shows as active until deleted. The Looker API 4.0 has full user/group/role endpoints (create, update incl. is_disabled, delete, set roles); every edition includes administrative API calls (Standard 1,000/month, Enterprise 10,000, Embed 100,000). Okta OIN app is SAML + SWA; Entra and JumpCloud are SSO-only. None by absence (rule 5).

scim.notes: No SCIM documented for Looker (original) or Looker (Google Cloud core).

auth.notes: API3 client ID/secret exchanged at the login endpoint for a short-lived token.

rate_limits.text: Administrative API calls per month: Standard 1,000; Enterprise 10,000; Embed 100,000.

limitations.text: Standard (and Viewer) user licences cannot use the Looker API interfaces; admins/developers can.

okta.notes: OIN page marks SAML and SWA only (read from page markup).

entra.notes: Entra "Looker Analytics Platform" is SSO with JIT; no provisioning tutorial.

google.notes: Looker (Google Cloud core) can use Google OAuth/IAM natively; no Google Workspace catalogue provisioning app checked.
